svg.title: Finite effacement and affine henselian comparison
svg.desc: An absolute integral closure of a polynomial integer ring supplies an integral surjective cover with vanishing finite constant cohomology on closed quotients. Integral finite-presentation models and continuity kill each class at a finite surjective stage. A constructible representative maps to an arbitrary torsion sheaf, embeds in enlarged finite constant direct images, and a pushout produces a monomorphism effacing that class. Induction then gives affine henselian cohomological comparison in every degree.
svg.metadata: Creator: GPT-6.1 Sol (OpenAI). CC0. Proof: Theorems J.1.7.1, J.2.4.1 and J.2.6.1. Free human comparisons: Stacks 09ZD, 09ZE, 09ZI.
svg.text: Exact maps for arbitrary affine bases and all torsion orders.
1. Kill a finite constant class at an actual finite stage
P = ℤ[xλ]; A = P/N; R is the integral closure of P in Ω.
Ω is algebraically closed; Frac R = Ω; B = R/NR.
B = colim Bi; every Spec Bi → Spec A is surjective.
Hq(ZB, M) = 0 for q > 0 and finite M.
Continuity makes the chosen class zero on some ZBᵢ.
2. Efface a torsion sheaf by the precise pushout
A class for F comes from a constructible C → F.
C embeds in enlarged finite direct images of finite constants C′.
F′ = (F ⊕ C′)/image(u, −v); the original class maps to zero.
C → F may have a kernel. The embedding C → C′ is what is used.
3. Compare every degree on the affine henselian pair
(A, I) is any henselian pair; F is any torsion étale sheaf.
q = 0: actual proper stage recovery and Noetherian sections.
q > 0: efface the class, then lift its lower-degree boundary.
No common annihilator or residue-characteristic restriction.
Proof: Theorems J.1.7.1, J.2.4.1 and J.2.6.1.
